ai.definition: Quantum Cryptography Networks are systems that utilize quantum mechanical phenomena, such as the principle of superposition and entanglement, to establish secure communication channels. These networks enable the creation of cryptographic keys that can be transmitted with absolute security, ensuring that any attempt to intercept or tamper with the information will be detected.
ai.howItWorks: Quantum cryptography networks use quantum key distribution (QKD) techniques. In QKD, a pair of entangled particles is generated and sent to two parties who wish to communicate securely. One party uses one particle while the other uses the other. By observing changes in the state of these particles due to their entanglement, both parties can generate a shared secret key that they use for encryption. Any attempt by an eavesdropper to intercept or measure the particles will cause detectable disturbances, alerting the communicating parties to potential security breaches.
ai.problemSolved: Traditional cryptographic systems are vulnerable to quantum computing attacks, which could potentially break widely used encryption methods like RSA and ECC. Quantum cryptography networks provide a solution that is theoretically unbreakable by any means, including those of quantum computers, due to the fundamental laws of physics governing the transmission and measurement of quantum states.
ai.manufacturing: Manufacturing quantum cryptography networks involves creating highly sensitive optical components, such as single-photon detectors and entangled photon sources. These components require precise fabrication techniques and materials that can operate at low temperatures and in vacuum environments to maintain their functionality.
ai.buildProcess: The build process includes the creation of entangled photon pairs using quantum light sources, the distribution of these photons over a network through optical fibers or free space, and the implementation of quantum key distribution protocols. This involves complex integration with classical communication infrastructure and sophisticated error correction mechanisms.
ai.costDrivers: High costs are driven by the need for specialized equipment such as single-photon detectors, entangled photon sources, and low-temperature cooling systems. Additionally, the complexity of integrating these technologies into existing networks adds to the overall cost.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The outlook is promising but faces significant challenges in scaling and commercialization. While there are early demonstrations and proof-of-concept implementations, widespread adoption will require overcoming technical hurdles related to reliability, distance limitations, and integration with existing communication systems.
ai.regulation: There are currently no specific regulations for quantum cryptography networks, though they may fall under broader cybersecurity frameworks. As the technology matures, dedicated regulatory guidelines may be developed to address its unique characteristics and applications.
ai.risks: Technical risks include maintaining the security of quantum keys over long distances due to signal attenuation and noise in optical fibers. There is also a risk that advancements in quantum computing could potentially find new ways to attack QKD systems. Additionally, there are logistical challenges related to the physical implementation of these networks, such as the need for specialized infrastructure and maintenance.
ai.profitability: Profitability is currently limited due to the early stage of development and high costs associated with research and deployment. However, as the technology matures and becomes more widely adopted, it could offer significant market opportunities in sectors requiring extremely secure communications, such as finance, government, and military.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future developments may focus on improving the distance over which quantum keys can be securely transmitted, enhancing the efficiency of QKD protocols, and developing new applications for quantum cryptography networks. Integration with other emerging technologies, such as blockchain, could also expand their utility and potential market reach.
ai.energyRequirements: Field units draw low hundreds of watts; fabrication is energy-intensive due to vacuum baking and cryogenic cooling requirements.

glossary.def: A method of secure key exchange that uses quantum mechanics to ensure the security of the communication channel.
The principle in quantum mechanics where a particle can exist in multiple states simultaneously until measured.
A phenomenon in which pairs or groups of particles interact in such a way that the state of one (no matter how far apart) is directly related to the state of another.

subsystems.name: Photon source
subsystems.role: creates the quantum states that carry the key, either as weak laser pulses or entangled photon pairs.
parts: nonlinear crystal for spontaneous parametric down-conversion

subsystems.name: Quantum channel
subsystems.role: transmits single photons with minimal loss and disturbance.

subsystems.name: Single-photon detectors
subsystems.role: detect individual photons, often at cryogenic temperatures.

subsystems.name: Classical channel
subsystems.role: carries basis and error-correction information, authenticated to block man-in-the-middle attacks.

subsystems.name: Post-processing and key management
subsystems.role: turns raw detections into a secret key and stores it for use.

subsystems.name: Nodes and repeaters
subsystems.role: extend range beyond a single point-to-point link.

buildSteps.title: Generate quantum states
buildSteps.detail: A laser produces very weak pulses (or a nonlinear crystal produces entangled photon pairs) encoded in polarisation or phase.

buildSteps.title: Transmit through the quantum channel
buildSteps.detail: Photons travel through optical fibre or free space to the receiving station.

buildSteps.title: Measure at the receiver
buildSteps.detail: The receiver randomly chooses a measurement basis and detects the arriving photons.

buildSteps.title: Sift and reconcile
buildSteps.detail: Sender and receiver compare bases over the classical channel and keep only the bits where they used the same basis.

buildSteps.title: Error correct
buildSteps.detail: Algorithms correct bit errors caused by noise in the channel or detectors.

buildSteps.title: Privacy amplify
buildSteps.detail: The key is compressed so that any information an eavesdropper might have is reduced to negligible levels.

buildSteps.title: Authenticate the classical channel
buildSteps.detail: A pre-shared secret or classical public-key cryptography ensures the classical messages cannot be altered by an attacker.

buildSteps.title: Use the key
buildSteps.detail: The resulting symmetric key feeds standard encryption, such as a one-time pad or AES, for secure communication.

buildSteps.title: Scale the network
buildSteps.detail: Trusted nodes or, in the future, quantum repeaters link multiple point-to-point segments to cover longer distances.

prerequisites.why: Needed to detect individual photons; current devices are bulky and often require cryogenic cooling, limiting practical deployment.
Required to extend quantum key distribution beyond a few hundred kilometres without relying on trusted nodes.
Needed to store quantum states inside repeaters long enough to perform entanglement swapping.
Prevents an eavesdropper from impersonating the sender or receiver on the classical channel.
Emerging standards aim to ensure interoperability between different vendors and network operators.

pathway.milestone: Point-to-point QKD links and trusted-node metro networks, such as the Beijing–Shanghai backbone in China.
pathway.unlocks: Secure key exchange for government, financial and critical-infrastructure links in metropolitan areas.

pathway.milestone: Satellite QKD, demonstrated by China's Micius satellite, and longer fibre links.
pathway.unlocks: Intercontinental key distribution where fibre is impractical.

pathway.milestone: Functional quantum repeaters and memories in the laboratory.
pathway.unlocks: Scalable long-distance quantum networks without trusted nodes.

pathway.milestone: Entanglement-based quantum internet with end-to-end entanglement distribution.
pathway.unlocks: Device-independent QKD and distributed quantum computing.
